_comment:
The exit. Crouch, HOLD the crouch, then leave the frame in a straight line up and out. Almost half the running time is spent coiled and motionless — that hold is the gag, because a character who simply moves off screen reads as a rendering bug, while a character who visibly winds up and THEN vanishes reads as a joke. The squash is a whole-actor `scaleBy` (it tweens, so the crouch is smooth) and the extra compress a frame before release is a `parts` transform (it snaps, so the release pops).

Deliberately NOT animated: any arc, any legs, any landing. There is no landing — that is what makes it an exit rather than a jump.

On ending hidden: visibility survives a cut, so `hide` here is a genuine lasting state and that is intended — the character has LEFT. But position and scale survive too, so both are restored to the mark at 1.70 while the character is already invisible. The exit costs exactly one thing (visibility) and nothing else, so a later shot that wants them back only has to show them, and they are standing where they belong at the size they belong.

Pure tier 1-3: whole-actor moves, one camera shake, two effects, two guaranteed sounds, ad-hoc transforms on `body`/`head`, two of the six faces. No clip, no pose, no new art.

beats._comment: the reason they are about to leave
the crouch begins. `scaleBy`, NEVER `scale` — staging puts characters at 0.62, so an absolute 0.88 would make them half again as big while supposedly ducking.
deepest coil, and a hair lower on the ground with it

the last compress before release, one snap rather than a tween — the visual equivalent of the intake of breath. Everything between 0.60 and 1.04 is dead still on purpose: this is the anticipation, and it is longer than the launch it sets up.
up and OFF. Deliberately not eased: an eased move decelerates at the end, and nothing about leaving should slow down. The 1.05 is the stretch that pairs with the squash.
the puff left behind at ground level, which is the shot's evidence that somebody was standing here
gone. Late enough that the move has visibly carried them out of frame first — hiding too early reads as a pop, not an exit.
tidy-up under cover of invisibility: mark and scale restored so the only thing this gag leaves behind is the fact that they are not here
